concept: A perfect record is the story, so the design treats the carousel like a scorecard that refuses to break. The hero puts the context in grey (first season in Europe) and the punchline in white: five games, five wins. Slide 2 is one giant 5/5 for the history line. Slide 3 is a match log with minute stamps that shows the twist: a red card inside 25 minutes, then two subs build the winner. Slide 4 is the stat that should have sunk them, an xG bar chart where Celta's bar is three times longer, so 'out-created but still won' reads before any number does. The last slide looks ahead to Sunday and the club-record chance, then hands fans the debate. Football green, type and bars only: no player photos, no club crests.
caption:
First season in Europe. Five games. Five wins.

Bournemouth won 2-1 at Celta Vigo in the Europa League on Thursday night. Iago Aspas put Celta ahead on 19 minutes and Bafode Diakite was sent off soon after following a VAR review.

Ten men. Away in Spain. They still turned it round. Alvaro Rodriguez headed in Amine Adli's cross early in the second half. Then substitute Rayan finished Marcus Tavernier's pass on 78 minutes for his fourth Europa League goal this season.

Sky Sports and beIN Sports say Bournemouth are the first English club to win their first five games in major European competition. It is also 10 straight wins in all competitions. They lead the league phase on 15 points, two clear of Juventus.

The odd part: Celta had 1.83 xG from 20 shots. Bournemouth had 0.63 from 10.

Fulham away on Sunday is next. A win would be six Premier League wins in a row for the first time in the club's history.
